audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused EVM internals (gas repricing, opcode execution, stack/bitwise operations, transaction validation, tracing) as well as CL-related topics (difficulty adjustment with uncle accounting, inclusion list P2P gossip). The primary focus is EL state transition and validation logic.

in_scope: EVM Opcode Execution (environment, block, bitwise, stack)
Inclusion List P2P Gossip and Validation (EIP-7805)
out_of_scope: Beacon Chain state transitions beyond difficulty

threats: Send invalid blocks containing transactions from contract addresses
Submit inclusion lists with invalid signatures
Manipulate block timestamps for difficulty gaming

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component. A smart contract executing within the EVM is part of the system under audit, not an external entity. The actual external entity is whoever submitted the transaction that triggers this contract execution.
Internal state storage. Historical block hashes are stored within the node's state database and are not an external data source. They were validated at the time of block import.
Output-only consumer. This entity receives data FROM the system but does not send data INTO it. It does not cross a trust boundary in the inbound direction.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit transactions via public JSON-RPC. No authentication required. Transactions may contain malicious payloads, attempt address collision attacks (EIP-3607), or craft gas-sensitive operations to exploit repriced opcodes (EIP-1884). Maps to EXT-TX-SUBMITTER, EXT-CALLER, EXT-RPC-CLIENT from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via Debug/Trace RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Trace and simulation requests can trigger expensive computation. Even though debug endpoints may be access-controlled, the data content is untrusted. Maps to EXT-TRACE-REQUESTER, EXT-RPC-CLIENT from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (EL)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. They may propagate blocks containing invalid transactions (e.g., from contract addresses violating EIP-3607) or blocks with manipulated difficulty/timestamp values. Maps to EXT-NETWORK-PEER from EIP-3607.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via CL Gossipsub
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL gossip peers are unauthenticated at transport level. Messages require BLS signature verification and committee membership checks. Maps to EXT-GOSSIP-PEER, EXT-REQUESTING-PEER, EXT-NETWORK-PEER from EIP-7805.

trusted_external_entities.name: Mining Client via Stratum
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EthereumStratum/2.0.0 TCP Protocol (mining.hello, mining.subscribe, mining.authorize, mining.submit)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Mining clients connect over TCP with session-based authentication (worker tokens). However, the channel is not encrypted by default and message content (solutions, session IDs) must be fully validated. Maps to EXT-MINER from EIP-1571.

trusted_external_entities.name: Mining Pool Server via Stratum
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Pool servers distribute work to miners. A malicious pool could send invalid jobs, manipulate difficulty targets, or provide incorrect epoch/extranonce data. No cryptographic authentication of server identity. Maps to EXT-POOL-SERVER from EIP-1571.

trusted_external_entities.name: Stratum Protocol Participant
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Either side of the Stratum connection can send malformed JSON, invalid hex formatting, or unauthorized messages. All protocol messages must be validated. Maps to EXT-CLIENT from EIP-1571.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Miner/Validator)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header fields (timestamp, coinbase, difficulty, uncles, PREVRANDAO)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers set block-level context values consumed by EVM opcodes. A malicious proposer can manipulate timestamps (within bounds) to affect difficulty calculations (EIP-100), set PREVRANDAO to influence randomness-dependent contracts, or include uncle references to game issuance. Maps to EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER, EXT-ATTACKER-MINER, EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Address Collision Attacker
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_sendRawTransaction with collision address as sender
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Sophisticated attacker with ~2^80 compute resources attempting to find an address collision between an EOA private key and a contract deployment address. EIP-3607 mitigates this by rejecting transactions from addresses with deployed code. Maps to EXT-ATTACKER from EIP-3607.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature recovery, nonce check, EIP-3607 sender code hash check (CodeHash == EMPTYCODEHASH), gas limit validation with EIP-1884 repriced opcodes, balance sufficiency check.
Trace requests must be rate-limited. eth_call/eth_estimateGas bypass EIP-3607 checks for simulation purposes. Resource consumption must be bounded to prevent DoS.

All transactions in received blocks must pass EIP-3607 sender validation. Block difficulty must be recomputed using EIP-100 formula. Timestamp bounds must be enforced. Blocks with invalid transactions must be rejected entirely.

Messages must pass: (1) REJECT checks: tx size <= MAX_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST, valid slot, committee membership, BLS signature verification. (2) IGNORE checks: timing constraints, committee root match, per-validator submission limit (max 2 per slot). REJECT failures penalize peer score.
Request parameters (slot, committee_indices bitvector) must be validated. Response size bounded to MAX_REQUEST_INCLUSION_LIST (16). Must not serve stale or unvalidated inclusion lists.

All JSON messages must be validated for format, type, and hex encoding. Worker credentials must be verified. Session IDs must be unpredictable. Error counts must be tracked with maxerrors disconnect threshold. Idle timeout must be enforced.
Solution submissions must validate: worker token authorization, job ID matches active job, nonce validity, and hash meets target difficulty. Stale/invalid submissions increment error counter.
Mining clients should validate epoch parameters, target difficulty values, extranonce bounds (max 6 bytes), and header hash format. Stale job indicators must be honored.

All messages must pass: JSON format validation (LF terminated), message type classification (request/response/notification), hex format validation (lowercase, no 0x prefix, minimal digits). Invalid messages return error codes: 2xx conditional, 3xx auth, 4xx syntax, 5xx server.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block Header Fields → EVM Execution Context (COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block timestamp must be within acceptable bounds relative to parent (used in EIP-100 difficulty calculation). Uncle references must be cryptographically verifiable via unclesHash. PREVRANDAO source must be the parent beacon block randao_mix. Difficulty must match EIP-100 formula: max((uncle_factor) - ((timestamp - parent.timestamp) // 9), -99).

After nonce verification, sender's CodeHash must be checked against EMPTYCODEHASH (0xc5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470). Any transaction from an address with deployed code must be rejected. This check must be applied consistently across all clients to prevent consensus failures.
